lines: I am Buys-The-Months, a broker. This is my ship, moored below Hereguard Plantation. Lilmoth lies a fair way east along the shore.
The water at Lilmoth is too shallow for a ship her size, so she lies here. The Argonians in her hold are an Owing gang. Each of them works off months of work owed for a debt or a wrong.

I keep those months written on my work roll, and I hire the gang out to unload the lighters, the cargo boats, at Lilmoth's dock. You came down the estuary with them, but you are on no line of my roll.
You owe me nothing, so I cannot hire you out. You are no affair of mine. Get off my ship.

infos.prompt: Where can I find work, then?
lines: I have no work for you. Salts-The-Catch keeps a house in Lilmoth. She asked me for anyone off my ship who saw the camp burn.
A guest of hers, Nesh-Deeka, pays for work. Go to Nesh-Deeka. Keep to the shore going east, a fair way. You pass the old lighthouse, and then you are in Lilmoth.
Keep on until you reach the second of the big ships, the one at anchor off Lilmoth's own dock. Salts-The-Catch's house is south of that ship, beside a wooden walkway.
I am Buys-The-Months. I have said all I will. You are on no line of my roll, so leave my ship.
Salts-The-Catch keeps her house south of the second big ship, below Lilmoth Dock, beside a wooden walkway. Nesh-Deeka is in there.
You again. You are on no line of my roll. Leave my ship.
I am Dives-Without-A-Rope. My family belongs to Nine Bends, a Hist, one of the great sacred trees of my people. I have been years away from it. Look at my colour. It has thinned for want of the tree.
Here I eat and I sleep. If you want to know about the camp, ask Wuleen-Sei.

infos.prompt: Buys-The-Months says you pay for anyone off his ship.
lines: Sit. Salts-The-Catch told me what Buys-The-Months said of you. I am Nesh-Deeka, and I do not lie well to a face, so I will tell you plainly. Two nights ago the gang's camp up the estuary burned.
A woman with a knotted cord at her wrist killed the courier who walked with the gang. She took his satchel. The satchel was mine.
Her people also cut the camp's Hist cutting, a slip of the sacred tree from which the families draw their lives. They cut it away from the eggs at its roots. The eggs died.
The gang say she looked at you lying by the fire and let you live. I serve the Veiled Reed, the quiet service of the An-Xileel, the state that rules Black Marsh. Do not say that name to a stranger.
Not here, not where others can hear. I have work for a hand whose name is on no roll. Ask me whatever you like about it before you answer. I will tell you what I can, and where I am holding back.
Come in. Salts-The-Catch described you to me. You are the one the gang carried aboard Buys-The-Months's ship, off the bank by the fire, the night their camp burned.
That same night a woman with a knotted cord at her wrist killed the courier who walked with the gang. She took his satchel. The satchel was mine.
Her people also cut the camp's Hist cutting, a slip of the sacred tree from which the families draw their lives. They cut it away from the eggs at its roots. The eggs died.
The gang say she saw you by the fire and let you live. I serve the Veiled Reed, the quiet service of the An-Xileel, the state that rules Black Marsh. Do not say that name to a stranger.
I need a hand whose name is on no roll, and you may be that hand. Ask me what you like before you answer. I will not lie to you about what I keep back.

infos.prompt: Who was the woman with the knotted cord?
lines: I do not know her name. We have heard of a small band that cuts a Hist's roots and draws the sap into jars. The camp is the first of its work that we have seen.
Why she spared a stranger, I cannot say. I would like to know. I think you would too.
We watch for cults, smugglers and killers who would harm the state or the trees. We work from houses like this one. My people wear no mark. You would not know one of us across a room.
That is what makes us useful. It is also what I would fear, if I were you. Most of what we stop deserves stopping. I do not say all of it. I am not sure of it.

infos.prompt: Why would the Reed want me?
lines: Because your name is on no roll. No family, broker or village will ask after you, so if you are taken, we never knew you. I will not dress that up. The woman who spared you is the one we are after.
You have a reason of your own to look for her. I would like you to look with your eyes open.
Fifty gold in your palm the moment you say yes, and my door here stays open to you after.
It is little against what the work may cost you. I will not tell you otherwise.

infos.prompt: Who does the Reed answer to?
lines: To the An-Xileel's offices at Stormhold, the state's city in the north-west. We answer to those offices alone. No tree, village or court has a say in what we do.
The people of those places never see our work. I have thought for years about whether that is a strength. I still cannot say.

infos.prompt: Was the courier who died at the camp one of yours?
lines: Yes. Mee-Tuja walked with the gang as our cover. His name was on no roll, as yours is not. He is dead now. The Reed will not own his body or his name. That is the price of working for us.
I will not pretend it is anything else.

infos.prompt: What are you not telling me?
lines: Two things. I will not name them. I do not lie well to a face, so I tell you where the gap is. If you found it later, you would call me a liar. Weigh that before you answer.

infos.prompt: I will work for the Reed.
lines: Good. We pay our hands, so here is the first of it, fifty gold. Now the first work. Buys-The-Months told Salts-The-Catch that Dives-Without-A-Rope, one of his gang, carried a jar aboard his ship.
The cutters, the people who cut the Hist's roots, dropped it by the fire. Dives-Without-A-Rope will not let it go. Bring me that jar from the ship's hold.
The ship is the one you were carried to, west of town past the old lighthouse. How you take it from her is your affair. Keep the Reed's name out of it.
Then my offer stands. It costs you nothing to leave it standing. I will be in this house. There is no other work on the dock for a stranger. Walk Lilmoth if you must. Come back to me.
I am Salts-The-Catch. I keep this house below Lilmoth Dock. I ask nothing of my guests. Nesh-Deeka is in this house.
I am Ux-Xeek, the broker's port hand.
You are not on my roll, so I have no time for you.
You are in the hold of a ship. It belongs to Buys-The-Months, a broker who hires out the work of others. The ship is moored below Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth.
I am Wuleen-Sei, his overseer. My gang carried you aboard, hurt, from the bank by the fire at our camp, the night it burned. We brought you down the estuary in our longboat.
Go up the stairs and out of the door onto the deck. Buys-The-Months waits there. Ask him what is owed in this hold, and why. That is for him to say, not me.
Raiders came off the water in the dark, two nights ago. Then the huts burned.
I was getting my gang into the longboat by torchlight. I never saw the raiders' faces.
Who they were, and what they took, I cannot tell you. Ask in Lilmoth. Others there know more than a broker's overseer.
